free_tier.stated: No quota and no account. 'All Veilid applications running veilid-core are nodes, and they are all equal in the eyes of the network. No nodes are special. Nodes are only limited by the resources they bring.'.

egress.terms: Free. Peer-to-peer, with inbound/outbound relays only for reachability.

record.interface_detail: AppMessage / AppCall primitives over routes; the core never parses app bytes. DHT for storage of small records.
record.tooling: veilid-core in Rust with bindings; veilid-server binary.
record.chaining: Not a file transport. Designed mobile-first for 'intermittent network connections, volatile IP addresses, CGNAT, limited storage and bandwidth'. The opposite of a bulk path.

limits.value: applications running veilid-core are nodes, and they are all equal in the eyes of the netwo

record.limits_note: No congestion control implemented. Open issue #404 'congestion control could be implemented with NodeStatus'; relay throttling is a to-do, not a feature.
record.reliability_note: sending bulk data through Veilid is unsupported in practice: without flow control a large transfer either starves or gets dropped. Eliminated on reliability, not on quota.

evidence.proved: 'No nodes are special ... Nodes are only limited by the resources they bring and the configuration of the network they are on'
'congestion control could be implemented with NodeStatus'; 'max bytes a flow can consume in X minutes' proposed as an unimplemented idea
'Relay traffic could use bandwidth throttling or roundrobin assignments' listed as To do
'limited storage and bandwidth' as a design assumption (mobile-first)

record.notes: No quota and no account. 'All Veilid applications running veilid-core are nodes, and they are all equal in the eyes of the network. No nodes are special. Nodes are only limited by the resources they bring.'.
